title: Clarence Williams and the Chicago picnic; calling each other 'cuz'
summary: Clarence Williams was connected to Columbia and OKeh. She tells how he got stage fright at a big Chicago event and played in the wrong key. The musicians all called each other 'cuz'.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: What about Clarence Williams? Was he a big man in Columbia and okay? When you knew him? What was his connection?

Well he had connections on all the records He featured Sarah Martin that was his one of his feature singers Sarah Martin and of course his wife done quite a bit Eva Taylor Eva Taylor she done quite a bit of records for him and with him But I used to work with him quite a bit in Chicago We worked at White City him and I together stuff with stuff

Irish Celtic Association, their big yearly event. I forget how many thousand people they told us was out there. And every music publisher in Chicago went out there to do a number, you know. Every song that they were plugging, you know, each company went out there to plug their number. So Clarence took me to go with him to plug his number, Royal Garden Blues. And when we got out there, he got stage fright. When he seen all them people out there, he started playing in another key. But I had been so used to singing, you know, Royal Garden Blues and the key that I said, I just went on singing, and by the time he caught me, I was about near the chorus. But the people realized it because soon when he caught up with me, they were playing, you know. And finally, he got through, I said, what was wrong with you, cuz? He said, I guess I got excited, all them people out there.

Cuz. That's what all of them, Joe Alvost, Armstrong, Louis Armstrong, we all used to call people one another cuz. We say cuz, you know, that was the cats, and like they say now, we call them cuz. They used to say cuz.
